skill.name: spawn-terminal
skill.description: Open a separate terminal for user-requested, non-AI CLI commands after checking command help output.
skill.summary: Runs non-AI CLI commands in a new terminal through a shared helper workflow.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally enables generic CLI command execution in a new terminal, so the core external command findings are confirmed. The filesystem findings are also confirmed because the instructions reference a helper through a parent-directory path. No prompt injection, covert exfiltration language, or separate semantic abuse pattern was found.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation for each command, add clear deny rules for destructive commands, and avoid running commands from untrusted directories.
Package the helper inside the skill folder or call a documented installed API instead of instructing agents to read ../agent/fork_terminal.py.

remediation.issue: Help check still executes user-selected commands
remediation.suggestion: Prefer trusted documentation for syntax checks, and treat help commands as execution that needs the same confirmation policy as full commands.

content.user_title: Spawn CLI Commands in a New Terminal
content.value_statement: Agents often need to run long CLI tasks without blocking their main session. This skill opens a separate terminal and routes non-AI commands through a shared helper.
actual_capabilities: Identifies user-requested non-AI CLI commands before execution.
Requires checking command help output before running the full command.
Opens a separate terminal through fork_terminal().
Supports optional log file output and blocking capture modes.
Directs AI agent requests to a separate spawn:agent workflow.
limitations: It does not validate command safety beyond the help-check workflow.
It depends on a fork_terminal helper outside this skill folder.
It is not for spawning Claude, Codex, or other AI agents.
It does not provide an allowlist for destructive commands.

use_cases.title: Run Build Tasks
use_cases.description: Start npm, Python, or build commands in another terminal while the main session stays available.

use_cases.title: Inspect CLI Syntax
use_cases.description: Check command help output before running a longer terminal task.

use_cases.title: Capture Debug Output
use_cases.description: Run a command with logging when full terminal output is useful for troubleshooting.

output_examples.input: A user asks to run a project build in a new terminal.
output_examples.output: The skill checks the command help output, opens a separate terminal, and reports that the build is running.

output_examples.input: A user asks to convert a media file and keep diagnostic output.
output_examples.output: The skill verifies the tool options, launches the conversion in another terminal, and enables log file capture.

output_examples.input: A user asks to start Claude Code in a new terminal.
output_examples.output: The skill refuses that workflow and routes the request to the separate AI agent spawning skill.

best_practices: Confirm the request is for a non-AI CLI command before using this skill.
Review help output before running the full command.
Use logging when command output is needed for troubleshooting.
anti_patterns: Running destructive commands without explicit user confirmation.
Using this skill to start Claude, Codex, or another AI agent.
Skipping the help step because the command looks familiar.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It opens a new terminal and runs a user-requested, non-AI CLI command through fork_terminal().

faq.question: Can it run AI agents?
faq.answer: No. Requests for Claude, Codex, Claude Code, or similar agents should use the separate spawn:agent workflow.

faq.question: Why does it check help output first?
faq.answer: The workflow uses help output to verify command syntax before launching the full terminal task.

faq.question: Can it capture output?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented helper supports log file output and blocking capture when those options are enabled.

faq.question: Is command execution restricted?
faq.answer: The skill separates AI and non-AI requests, but it does not define a command allowlist or strong safety policy.

faq.question: What is the main security concern?
faq.answer: The main concern is arbitrary CLI execution, especially when commands are destructive or come from untrusted project paths.
